claims.text: Greg Short reports that at a high level of competitive success, peer-level competition effectively disappears, requiring a self-generated motivation mechanism: deliberately manufacturing imaginary rivals (people perceived as talking negatively, competitors believed to be trying) to sustain competitive drive. Without this manufactured competition, the motivational edge erodes.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: Speaker has reached a level where no meaningful peer-level competitors exist in their market
claims.mechanism: When no real competition is visible, the competitive drive that originally motivated action loses its object; manufacturing a rival restores the felt pressure that sustains peak performance.
bounded_by: Only applies when the speaker has already reached a level of dominance where real competition is sparse; early-stage operators have abundant real competition and do not need this mechanism

claims.text: Greg Short cites George (a UK-based fashion brand founder with ~100 employees) as evidence that authentic community building without paid advertising volume or growth hacking tactics can sustain a business at significant scale. George designs every piece himself and embraces his community rather than relying on high-volume Facebook ads or secret marketing tricks.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: Fashion or physical product brand where the founder's taste and identity are core to the product

numbers.axis: business scale achieved through authentic community building vs. ad-volume tactics

anchors.region: George's approach (no heavy ads, founder-designed product, community focus)
implied alternative (growth hacking, thousands of Facebook ads)
anchors.value: not cited as necessary for comparable scale

bounded_by: Speaker presents this as a specific observed case, not a controlled comparison; no baseline of what ad-heavy competitors at the same scale look like is given

examples.text: Greg Short describes George, a UK fashion brand founder who spends most of his time in LA and runs approximately 100 employees in the UK. George designs every piece of clothing himself, does not use heavy Facebook ad volumes or growth hacking tricks, and instead focuses entirely on building and embracing his community. Greg Short holds George up as an exemplar of authentic execution.

practices.text: When you have reached a level where no real peer-level competitors exist, manufacture competition by focusing on critics or perceived rivals to maintain competitive sharpness.
